title: Jarren Duran: ‘I thought I was going to be released’ by Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran believed he might be released amid his struggles with the Boston Red Sox this season.
Despite batting .200, Duran remains with the Red Sox for the stretch run, contributing to their recent 14-2 win.
Boston kept Duran through the trade deadline despite acquiring another outfielder and linked trade rumors.

title: Wu, Councilor Louijeune lead more than 100 elected officials in urging Congress to extend protections for Haitians
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Mayor Michelle Wu and Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune lead over 100 officials urging Congress to extend TPS for Haitians.
Officials sent a letter to the Senate advocating for a TPS extension through 2029, following a Supreme Court ruling.
Ending TPS is seen as destabilizing, with Haitian TPS holders contributing up to $5.9 billion annually to the U.S. economy.

title: Durbin hits grand slam and Abreu goes deep twice as streaking Red Sox rout White Sox 14-2
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Caleb Durbin's grand slam led the Red Sox to a 14-2 victory over the White Sox at Fenway Park.
Wilyer Abreu hit two solo home runs, contributing to Boston's surge of winning 24 of their last 27 games.
Patrick Sandoval earned his first major league win since 2024, pitching five-plus innings with five strikeouts.

title: What Adley Rutschman said about joining Red Sox after blockbuster trade
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman joins the Red Sox after a trade from Baltimore involving Carlos Narvaez and several prospects.
Rutschman is recovering from wrist inflammation; his return to playing is pending a medical evaluation and rehab stint.
Rutschman's addition strengthens Boston's catching with his defensive skills and potential batting power.

title: Lawsuit against Suffolk DA, BPD aims to force release of footage of fatal police shooting in Roxbury
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A lawsuit filed against the Boston Police and Suffolk DA's office demands release of footage from a fatal Roxbury police shooting.
Boston Police Officer Nicholas O'Malley, charged with manslaughter, shot Stephenson King during a reported carjacking incident in March.
Authorities denied footage requests, citing ongoing investigations, while the nonprofit argues for transparency under public records law.

title: Could Roman Anthony, Garrett Crochet return to Red Sox this season?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Roman Anthony resumed batting practice as he rehabs a wrist sprain and torn ligament in his finger.
Garrett Crochet has started throwing again after over three months sidelined due to shoulder inflammation and a lat strain.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy says a return this season is possible for both Anthony and Crochet if recovery progresses.

title: ‘We’ve got to make up for lost time’: After lengthy absence, Gabe Jacas faces a new challenge
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Gabe Jacas signed a 4-year deal with the Patriots worth up to $8.6 million after lengthy contract negotiations.
Jacas delayed joining team activities due to concerns about a knee procedure, but is now participating in training camp.
Coach Mike Vrabel emphasized the need for Jacas to catch up, acknowledging his eagerness and successful acclimation process.

title: Skeletal remains found in South Boston home turn out to be animal bones, police say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Police found skeletal remains in a South Boston home, initially uncertain if human or animal.
The bones were identified as animal remains by the state medical examiner's office.
A bag with shoes was discovered near the bones; investigation remains active.

title: Drake Maye, offense finish strong and other takeaways from Day 9 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye finishes strong, completing 11 of his final 12 passes during Patriots training camp Day 9.
DeMario Douglas emerges as a key player in the Patriots' offense, primarily operating out of the slot.
A.J. Brown dislocates his thumb but remains a full participant, impressing coaches with competitiveness.

title: Family of Abington teen killed in crash during police chase says car was not stolen
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Sebastian Hamilton, 17, was killed in a crash during a police chase in Abington involving a reported stolen SUV.
Hamilton drove the SUV after a teen passenger allegedly took the vehicle without the parent's permission.
The officer involved in pursuing the SUV is on leave, as the crash is under investigation by local police.
